propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events breaks cross-clone merges via git rename detection pairing but reclaims no repository space since blobs persist in git history

The queue reduce reads all matching files per type per ticket making it O(history), while digest lookup is already O(1) and the actual bottleneck is unbounded file opens in pending_enrichment gate checks

A read-bound design using newest-first suffix scans of lexicographically ordered timestamp-prefixed filenames can reduce file opens from 4977 to 1658 per full-store scan without violating append-only semantics or invariant I1
Merge-safe retention must rename to deterministic source-derived paths with identical content; deletion paired with fresh-UUID adds violates reconvergence guarantees
The design is verified as merge-safe by unchanged behavior against existing two-clone regression tests and requires no physical deletes or renames of committed events
